label: Teltonika RUT240
description: A palm-sized 4G LTE Cat 4 router: one WAN port that can be reconfigured as LAN, one LAN port, both 10/100, and 2.4 GHz 802.11b/g/n Wi-Fi. The box that gets put in a cabinet when a site needs a cellular uplink and nothing else.
notes: Vendor figures from the RUT240 datasheet v1.2: 1 x WAN port 10/100 Mbps (can be configured to LAN), 1 x LAN port 10/100 Mbps, both IEEE 802.3/802.3u; Wi-Fi 802.11b/g/n in AP and STA modes; 4G LTE Cat 4. The WAN port is modelled separately because Teltonika ships it as WAN and lets you reassign it - a lab that needs two LAN ports on this box is a supported configuration, not a mistake.

label: Teltonika RUT950
description: A 4G LTE Cat 4 router with four 10/100 ports (one WAN, three LAN) and 2.4 GHz 802.11b/g/n Wi-Fi. The four-port cellular router that predates the RUT956 in the same rack slot.
notes: Vendor figures from the RUT950 datasheet v1.1: 1 x WAN port (can be configured to LAN) 10/100 Mbps and 3 x LAN ports 10/100 Mbps, IEEE 802.3/802.3u; Wi-Fi 802.11b/g/n in AP and STA modes; 4G LTE Cat 4 with dual SIM. Same port shape as the RUT956 but without the serial ports and I/O block.

label: Teltonika RUTX11
description: A 4G LTE Cat 6 router with four Gigabit ports (one WAN, three LAN) and dual-band 802.11ac Wave 2 Wi-Fi at up to 867 Mbps. The gigabit step up from the RUT950, with the same four-port faceplate.
notes: Vendor figures from the RUTX11 datasheet v1.4: 1 x WAN port 10/100/1000 Mbps and 3 x LAN ports 10/100/1000 Mbps, IEEE 802.3/802.3u/802.3az with auto MDI/MDIX; Wi-Fi 802.11b/g/n/ac Wave 2 (Wi-Fi 5) dual band at up to 867 Mbps; 4G LTE Cat 6 (300 Mbps downlink class), which is why wwan0 is modelled at 300M rather than the 100M of the Cat 4 units.
